question.text: 'Himalaya Mezzanine Debt AIF' has only 8 LPs, each of whom has committed ₹85 crore. Under the PPM framework, what exemption pathway is available to this fund?

answer.text: Exemption from the minimum prescribed PPM disclosures and annual audit, provided each investor commits at least ₹70 crore (USD 10 million) and also provides a waiver to the fund in the prescribed manner.
Automatic exemption from the PPM filing and annual audit requirements.
Exemption only from SEBI's comments on the PPM, but annual audit remains mandatory.
No exemption — the fund must comply with all PPM disclosures and audit obligations regardless of commitment size.

explanation.text: The Logic: The chapter specifies that AIFs/schemes in which each investor commits a minimum of ₹70 crore (USD 10 million or equivalent in non-INR currency) AND the investor provides a waiver to the fund from the requirement of PPM in SEBI prescribed template and annual audit of terms of PPM — in the prescribed manner — are exempt. 'Automatic' without waiver is WRONG; LVF is a different exemption basis. The Trap: Exemption is not automatic — the waiver has to be affirmatively provided by each LP. Partial exemption (only from SEBI comments) is not the framework. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests this threshold identically. The ₹70 crore floor mirrors USD 10 million because the Regulations cap AIF large-ticket investor concessions at that global equivalent. Manager's Pro-Tip: Before relying on the waiver route, obtain the waiver in writing at the Contribution Agreement stage — retro-fitting after first-close invites LP pushback and may invalidate the fund's audit holiday.
